text:
The Canadiens are 12-5-4 with 28 points, a good place to be in late November, and nobody in Montreal is relaxed about it. Ivan Demidov hasn't played since a preseason ankle injury, Cole Caufield's criticism of the officiating drew a public reply from an NHL referee (per Markerzone), and the power play has gone from a talking point to a problem. On Monday, hours after Nick Suzuki said it was "definitely not broken," it went 0 for 4 at Madison Square Garden (as Sportsnet's Eric Engels noted) in a 3-1 loss.

Here is the uncomfortable part: the standings flatter them. Montreal has only 48.41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and allows 3.47 per 60 minutes. Its goaltending has saved 9.79 more goals than the shots deserved, and by our count the Canadiens have about 6.4 more points than their play has earned. Our projection still gives them a 60% playoff chance and about 95 points, but that depends on the saves continuing.

The best line has been the checkers: Phillip Danault between Alexandre Texier and Zachary Bolduc has controlled 61% of the expected goals. Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson drive play as a pair, at 57%. The worry is Juraj Slafkovský, with five points in ten games against 7.8 expected, and a second pair (Alexandre Carrier and Kaiden Guhle) at 41%.

What to watch: whether the chances catch up to the record before the goaltending stops covering the gap.
headline: Montreal's record is ahead of its game
